Logitech launches Gen 2 suite to tackle boardroom tech friction
Unoptimized Boardrooms Costing Australian Workplaces Billions
Australian businesses are facing financial and cultural costs as video conferencing technology fails to keep pace with the widespread adoption of hybrid work. Logitech estimates that 85 percent of boardrooms across the country remain unoptimized for video calls, creating a persistent drain on corporate productivity and employee well-being.
-
The Tech TL;DR:
- Logitech research estimates 85% of boardrooms lack proper video conferencing optimization, costing companies significant time and money.
- Unreliable meeting tech leads to a median productivity loss of 12.2 minutes per person per meeting, with TPG Telecom commissioning data estimating annual SME losses at $3.75 billion.
- The new Logitech Gen 2 product suite aims to address hardware friction through AI-driven audio, automated scheduling, and centralized room-health telemetry.
The 12-Minute Productivity Tax Per Meeting
White-collar employees routinely spend the first five to ten minutes of a scheduled call troubleshooting equipment. Laptops fail to handshake with displays, audio drivers drop out, and uncooperative cameras stall proceedings while remote participants wait.
Mood Degradation and the Cost of Outdated Hardware
The friction of legacy hardware extends beyond lost hours during the working day. Logitech’s ‘Ctrl Tomorrow’ study shows that 64 percent of Australian consumers and IT decision-makers experience a lingering impact on their mood after hours due to frustrating office technology. Conversely, 79 percent of surveyed workers report achieving peak focus and performance when their AV setups work without technical issues.
With virtually all corporate meetings now incorporating at least one remote participant, enterprises are forced to re-evaluate capital expenditure on legacy systems. Upgrading infrastructure requires proving a clear return on investment, yet the cost of standing still becomes quantifiable with every failed connection.
Hardware Architecture of the Logitech Gen 2 Suite
To mitigate these recurring failure points, Logitech developed its Gen 2 hardware portfolio to span environments from compact huddle spaces to complex, multi-microphone boardrooms. The line-up introduces the Logitech Rally Bar 2, an all-in-one video bar featuring an aluminum unibody construction—a first for the manufacturer’s video bar category—and integrated AI-powered noise suppression algorithms.
The hardware ecosystem also includes the Tap Scheduler 2 panel for real-time room availability signaling and the Tap IP 2 network-connected meeting controller. These units feature native deep integrations with major collaboration platforms, including Microsoft Teams, Zoom, and Google Meet. The Rally Bar 2 incorporates environmental sensor technology derived from Logitech Spot, which measures meeting room telemetry and equips facility leaders with utilization metrics to assess workplace health.
